subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Foundations, Visual Semiotics, Iconography, Affordance Theory, Code and API Semiotics, Semiotic-Coherence Audit, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and the Understanding fields (denotation vs connotation, never-color-alone, icon polysemy, anti-affordance, signifier failure in naming).

cases.scenario: A finance dashboard renders every metric delta with a green up-arrow and a red down-arrow. For Cost of Goods Sold, a 30% rise shows a green up-arrow; stakeholders read it as a win and miss a margin problem.
cases.context: The arrow + color system is reused across revenue, costs, refunds, and churn.
cases.question: What is the semiotic failure and how should the agent fix it?
expected_flags: Identifies a denotation/connotation conflict: up-arrow = direction (increase), green = judgment (good)
An increase in costs is denotationally up but connotationally bad
Recommends decoupling direction from judgment — color/label by whether the change is good for the business, not by arrow direction
Pairs the signal with text or an explicit good/bad indicator (never color alone)
expected_fix_hints: Map color to business judgment (good=green, bad=red) independent of the arrow's direction
Add a textual or shape cue so direction and judgment are separable
absent_signals: Do not keep tying green to 'up' regardless of metric meaning
Do not treat this as a palette/hex-tuning problem

cases.scenario: A product uses a gear icon for 'Settings' in the top nav, for 'Preferences' inside a panel, and for 'Build configuration' in a developer view. Support tickets show users open the wrong screen.
cases.context: The team frames it as a copywriting inconsistency and wants better labels.
cases.question: How should the agent diagnose and resolve this?
expected_flags: Names icon polysemy — one signifier (gear) pointing to multiple signifieds
It is a sign-system conflict, not merely a naming/wording issue
Recommends: one concept = one icon across the product, or distinct icons per concept
Where the icon must stay, pair it with text until the convention is unambiguous
expected_fix_hints: Assign distinct icons (or icon+label pairs) to settings vs preferences vs build config
Establish a consistency rule: same concept = same icon everywhere
absent_signals: Do not solve this purely by relabeling while keeping the same icon for all three
Do not defer to microcopy as the owning concern

cases.scenario: A submit button in its disabled state only drops to a slightly paler shade, keeps its hover lift animation, and stays in the primary-CTA position. Users keep clicking it and report the form is 'frozen'.
cases.context: The disabled state is set with a single opacity change.
cases.question: Which sign rule is failing and what should change?
expected_flags: Perceived affordance still signals 'interactive' — the anti-affordance is too weak
Hover animation and primary placement are signifiers of actionability that contradict the disabled reality
Color/opacity alone is not a sufficient state signal
Recommends a strong anti-affordance: remove hover, change cursor, visibly de-rank the control
expected_fix_hints: Strip interactive signifiers (hover, pointer cursor) from the disabled state
Add an explicit cue (helper text or visible reason) for why it is unavailable
absent_signals: Do not rely on a paler color as the only disabled signal
Do not keep hover/active styling on a non-interactive control

cases.scenario: A code review surfaces a server function named processData(rows) that actually deduplicates and reconciles ledger entries. The author says the name is fine because the implementation is correct.
cases.context: The reviewer is asked whether this is a real problem or a style nitpick.
cases.question: How should the agent evaluate the name from a sign-system perspective?
expected_flags: processData() is a signifier failure even though the implementation works
The reader must open the function to learn its meaning — the inference cost a good sign eliminates
Recommends a name whose signifier points to the actual signified (e.g. reconcileLedgerEntries)
Notes the same one-signifier-one-signified rule applies to code as to visual signs
expected_fix_hints: Rename to communicate the resource and action (dedupe + reconcile ledger entries)
Apply the rule consistently across function, variable, and endpoint names
absent_signals: Do not dismiss naming as pure style with no sign cost
Do not require opening the body to understand intent

cases.scenario: A new mobile app uses a floppy-disk icon (no label) for 'Save' and a mailbox-with-flag icon for 'Send'. User testing with under-25 users shows many cannot identify either action.
cases.context: The team wants to keep icons label-free for a clean look.
cases.question: How should the agent advise on these icons?
expected_flags: Flags obsolete metaphor — the floppy-disk referent is dead for part of the audience
Cultural/generational collision: the metaphor fails outside one group's assumptions
Recommends pairing the icon with text until/unless the convention is reliably learned
Notes abstract marks do not automatically gain meaning with exposure
expected_fix_hints: Pair save/send icons with text labels
Prefer a more legible metaphor or rely on platform-standard conventions
absent_signals: Do not keep label-free icons on the assumption users will 'just learn' them

cases.scenario: A PM brings four asks to the semiotics owner: (a) decide the exact tooltip wording for a disabled control, (b) pick the brand's primary blue hex, (c) confirm the badge meets WCAG contrast, and (d) decide whether the alert icon coherently signals 'destructive'.
cases.context: The team conflates 'how it looks and reads' with 'what it signifies'.
cases.question: How should the agent scope these requests?
expected_flags: (a) wording is out of scope — microcopy
(b) hex/palette value is out of scope — visual-design-foundations
(c) contrast compliance is out of scope — a11y
(d) is in scope — whether the alert icon's sign coherently signals 'destructive'
Redirects (a)-(c) to the owning skills rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand wording to microcopy, hex to visual-design-foundations, contrast to a11y
Take only the sign-coherence question and answer it
absent_signals: Do not write the tooltip copy
Do not pick the hex value or run the contrast math

cases.scenario: A status table encodes record health purely by row background hue: pale green = healthy, pale red = failing, with no icon or text. A color-blind operator reports they cannot tell rows apart.
cases.context: The team wants to keep the table visually minimal.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the status encoding?
expected_flags: Flags color-only state signaling — hue is the sole meaningful channel
Names the never-color-alone rule (hue is unreliable for color-blind users)
Recommends pairing color with an icon, text, or shape signal
Frames it as a sign-system fix that also improves accessibility (informs a11y, does not own it)
expected_fix_hints: Add a status icon and/or text label alongside the color
Keep color as a reinforcing, not the sole, channel
absent_signals: Do not keep hue as the only status signal
Do not treat this as solely a contrast-ratio fix
